messages:
maya: quick ping — PR #2410 up for perf/cost review. Changes: adaptive KV cache TTL + routing fallback + quantization flag for gpt-small. bench on r5g: tail latency (p95) down ~9%, tokens/sec +14%, cost/unit ~-6%. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2410

liam: taking a look now — can you paste the perf run command?

maya: sure:
```
./bench --model gpt-small --seq 1024 --concurrency 16 --runs 200 --quantize true --kv-ttl 300
```
raw numbers: p95 120ms -> 109ms, tokens/s 820 -> 935, cost estimate drop ~6% on avg.

olivia: two quick Qs: 1) does quantize=true change deterministic sampling? 2) routing fallback — what happens during cold starts?

maya: 1) no sampling changes, it's weight-only quant -> inference outputs identical for float32 vs quantized in our tests (within noise). 2) routing fallback hits a compatible lower-capacity variant in same region; we added a rate limiter to avoid thundering herd.

sam: looks reasonable. Can we add a short canary config? e.g., 10% traffic, 30m window, revert on latency+error spikes. Also add metric flags: kv_miss_rate, route_fallback_count.

maya: added canary in PR description and console rollout config. here's snippet:
```
canary:
  traffic: 10%
  window: 30m
  rollback_criteria:
    - p95_latency > baseline * 1.15
    - error_rate > baseline + 0.5%
```

paul: quick nit: please add comment in code about KV TTL heuristic, and add unit test for eviction boundary.

maya: will add tests + comment. anyone else? @liam can you approve if you don't see infra issues?

liam: LGTM modulo one logging line — I'll push an approve in a few and file a follow-up for log cleanup.

deploy-bot: scheduled merge window at 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC for non-breaking perf patches :rocket:

maya: thanks all — merging after liam's approve and tests pass :pray:
